text: In 1856, quarriers working a cave in Germany’s Neander Valley discovered several mysterious fossils.
ipa: /ɪn 1856 quarriers wˈɝkɪŋ ə kˈeɪv ɪn dʒˈɝməniz neander vˈæli dɪskˈʌvɚd sˈɛvɹəl mɪstˈɪɹiəs fˈɑsəlz/

text: The remains changed hands until being identified as the skullcap
ipa: /ðə ɹɪmˈeɪnz tʃˈeɪndʒd hˈændz əntˈɪl bˈiɪŋ aɪdˈɛntəfˌaɪd ˈæz ðə skˈʌlkˌæp/

text: and femur bones of something ancient and human, but not quite us.
ipa: /ənd fˈimɚ bˈoʊnz ˈʌv sˈʌmθɪŋ ˈeɪntʃənt ənd hjˈumən bˈʌt nˈɑt kwˈaɪt ˈʌs/

text: It soon became clear they belonged to an extinct human species— the first ever known
ipa: /ˈɪt sˈun bɪkˈeɪm klˈɪɹ ðˈeɪ bɪlˈɔŋd tˈu ˈæn ɪkstˈɪŋkt hjˈumən spˈiʃiz ðə fˈɝst ˈɛvɚ nˈoʊn/

text: to science: Homo neanderthalensis, or simply, Neanderthals.
ipa: /tˈu sˈaɪəns hˈoʊmoʊ neanderthalensis ˈɔɹ sˈɪmpli niˈændɚθˌɔlz/

text: Not long before the discovery, many believed the world was only about 6,000 years old.
ipa: /nˈɑt lˈɔŋ bɪfˈɔɹ ðə dɪskˈʌvɚi mˈɛni bɪlˈivd ðə wˈɝld wˈɑz ˈoʊnli əbˈaʊt 6000 jˈɪɹz ˈoʊld/

text: However, by the mid-1800s, naturalists were more comfortable with geological timelines and evolutionary theory.
ipa: /hˌaʊˈɛvɚ bˈaɪ ðə mid1800s nˈætʃɚəlɪsts wˈɝ mˈɔɹ kˈʌmfɚtəbəl wˈɪð dʒˌiəlˈɑdʒɪkəl tˈaɪmlaɪnz ənd ˌɛvəlˈuʃənˌɛɹi θˈɪɹi/

text: The idea that ancient remains could belong to another human species was finally becoming conceivable.
ipa: /ðə aɪdˈiə ðˈæt ˈeɪntʃənt ɹɪmˈeɪnz kˈʊd bɪlˈɔŋ tˈu ənˈʌðɚ hjˈumən spˈiʃiz wˈɑz fˈaɪnəli bɪkˈʌmɪŋ kənsˈivəbəl/

text: But misconceptions persisted, and much “Neander slander” ensued.
ipa: /bˈʌt mɪskənsˈɛpʃənz pɚsˈɪstɪd ənd mˈʌtʃ neander slˈændɚ ɪnsˈud/

text: Early on, Neanderthals were depicted as dim-witted oafs who died out
ipa: /ˈɝli ˈɑn niˈændɚθˌɔlz wˈɝ dɪpˈɪktəd ˈæz dimwitted oafs hˈu dˈaɪd ˈaʊt/

text: because of their inferiority to modern humans, aka Homo sapiens.
ipa: /bɪkˈɔz ˈʌv ðˈɛɹ ˌɪnfɪɹiˈɔɹɪtˌi tˈu mˈɑdɚn hjˈumənz ˈɑkə hˈoʊmoʊ sˈeɪpiənz/

text: One popular illustration suggested that, in addition to being hairy
ipa: /wˈʌn pˈɑpjəlɚ ˌɪləstɹˈeɪʃən sədʒˈɛstɪd ðˈæt ɪn ədˈɪʃən tˈu bˈiɪŋ hˈɛɹi/

text: and club-carrying, Neanderthals stooped and had ape-like opposable toes, even
ipa: /ənd clubcarrying niˈændɚθˌɔlz stˈupt ənd hˈæd ˈeɪplˌaɪk opposable tˈoʊz ˈivɪn/

text: though this wasn’t reflected in skeletal findings.
ipa: /ðˈoʊ ðˈɪs wasnt ɹɪflˈɛktɪd ɪn skˈɛlətəl fˈaɪndɪŋz/

text: Over the next century, however, archaeologists discovered more hominin species,
ipa: /ˈoʊvɚ ðə nˈɛkst sˈɛntʃɚi hˌaʊˈɛvɚ ˌɑɹkiˈɑlədʒɪsts dɪskˈʌvɚd mˈɔɹ hominin spˈiʃiz/

text: as well as the remains of over 300 Neanderthal individuals.
ipa: /ˈæz wˈɛl ˈæz ðə ɹɪmˈeɪnz ˈʌv ˈoʊvɚ 300 niˈændɚθˌɔl ˌɪndəvˈɪdʒəwəlz/

text: Compared to modern humans, Neanderthals had larger, deeper-set eyes; were shorter
ipa: /kəmpˈɛɹd tˈu mˈɑdɚn hjˈumənz niˈændɚθˌɔlz hˈæd lˈɑɹdʒɚ deeperset ˈaɪz wˈɝ ʃˈɔɹtɚ/

text: and more muscular had higher caloric needs with slightly bigger bodies, including their hearts and brains.
ipa: /ənd mˈɔɹ mˈʌskjəlɚ hˈæd hˈaɪɚ kəlˈɔɹɪk nˈidz wˈɪð slˈaɪtli bˈɪɡɚ bˈɑdiz ˌɪnklˈudɪŋ ðˈɛɹ hˈɑɹts ənd bɹˈeɪnz/

text: For over 350,000 years, they lived across Europe and Western Asia.
ipa: /fˈɔɹ ˈoʊvɚ 350000 jˈɪɹz ðˈeɪ lˈɪvd əkɹˈɔs jˈʊɹəp ənd wˈɛstɚn ˈeɪʒə/

text: For at least their final 10,000 years, they spatially overlapped with Homo sapiens.
ipa: /fˈɔɹ ˈæt lˈist ðˈɛɹ fˈaɪnəl 10000 jˈɪɹz ðˈeɪ spatially ˈoʊvɚlˌæpt wˈɪð hˈoʊmoʊ sˈeɪpiənz/

text: And archaeological finds have suggested that they led much more complex lives than initially suspected.
ipa: /ənd ˌɑɹkiəlˈɑdʒɪkəl fˈaɪndz hˈæv sədʒˈɛstɪd ðˈæt ðˈeɪ lˈɛd mˈʌtʃ mˈɔɹ kˈɑmplɛks lˈɪvz ðˈæn ˌɪnˈɪʃəli səspˈɛktɪd/

text: In the 1950s, scientists unearthed the remains of a Neanderthal in a cave in northern Iraq
ipa: /ɪn ðə 1950s sˈaɪəntɪsts ənˈɝθt ðə ɹɪmˈeɪnz ˈʌv ə niˈændɚθˌɔl ɪn ə kˈeɪv ɪn nˈɔɹðɚn ˌɪɹˈɑk/

text: who had a severed right arm, injured leg, and was likely partially blind and deaf.
ipa: /hˈu hˈæd ə sˈɛvɚd ɹˈaɪt ˈɑɹm ˈɪndʒɚd lˈɛɡ ənd wˈɑz lˈaɪkli pˈɑɹʃəli blˈaɪnd ənd dˈɛf/

text: Yet he survived long after these injuries, suggesting his community provided him extensive, daily support.
ipa: /jˈɛt hˈi sɚvˈaɪvd lˈɔŋ ˈæftɚ ðˈiz ˈɪndʒɚiz sədʒˈɛstɪŋ hˈɪz kəmjˈunəti pɹəvˈaɪdɪd hˈɪm ɪkstˈɛnsɪv dˈeɪli səpˈɔɹt/

text: And another skeleton from a French cave belonged to an older Neanderthal
ipa: /ənd ənˈʌðɚ skˈɛlətən fɹˈʌm ə fɹˈɛntʃ kˈeɪv bɪlˈɔŋd tˈu ˈæn ˈoʊldɚ niˈændɚθˌɔl/

text: who probably had trouble walking and had lost
ipa: /hˈu pɹˈɑbəblˌi hˈæd tɹˈʌbəl wˈɔkɪŋ ənd hˈæd lˈɔst/

text: so many teeth he may have needed his food ground up.
ipa: /sˈoʊ mˈɛni tˈiθ hˈi mˈeɪ hˈæv nˈidəd hˈɪz fˈud ɡɹˈaʊnd ˈʌp/

text: Both excavation sites also showed signs of burial, all suggesting
ipa: /bˈoʊθ ˌɛkskəvˈeɪʃən sˈaɪts ˈɔlsoʊ ʃˈoʊd sˈaɪnz ˈʌv bˈɛɹiəl ˈɔl sədʒˈɛstɪŋ/

text: that Neanderthals went beyond immediate, practical concerns for survival and cared for their ailing and dead.
ipa: /ðˈæt niˈændɚθˌɔlz wˈɛnt bɪˈɑnd ˌɪmˈidˌiət pɹˈæktəkəl kənsˈɝnz fˈɔɹ sɚvˈaɪvəl ənd kˈɛɹd fˈɔɹ ðˈɛɹ ˈeɪlɪŋ ənd dˈɛd/

text: Teeth analyses also indicate that Neanderthals might have used anti-inflammatory and antibiotic plants medicinally.
ipa: /tˈiθ ənˈæləsˌiz ˈɔlsoʊ ˈɪndəkˌeɪt ðˈæt niˈændɚθˌɔlz mˈaɪt hˈæv jˈuzd antiinflammatory ənd ˌæntibaɪˈɑtɪk plˈænts mədˈɪsənəli/

text: For a while, researchers assumed that Neanderthals hunted big game with unsophisticated, brute force ambush attacks.
ipa: /fˈɔɹ ə wˈaɪl ɹˈisɚtʃɚz əsˈumd ðˈæt niˈændɚθˌɔlz hˈʌntəd bˈɪɡ ɡˈeɪm wˈɪð ˌʌnsəfˈɪstɪkˌeɪtɪd bɹˈut fˈɔɹs ˈæmbˌʊʃ ətˈæks/

text: But cut marks on rabbit bones and tools with apparent traces of scales and feathers.
ipa: /bˈʌt kˈʌt mˈɑɹks ˈɑn ɹˈæbət bˈoʊnz ənd tˈulz wˈɪð əpˈɛɹənt tɹˈeɪsəz ˈʌv skˈeɪlz ənd fˈɛðɚz/

text: Suggest Neanderthals were capable of the skill required to capture small game, perhaps utilizing
ipa: /sədʒˈɛst niˈændɚθˌɔlz wˈɝ kˈeɪpəbəl ˈʌv ðə skˈɪl ɹikwˈaɪɚd tˈu kˈæptʃɚ smˈɔl ɡˈeɪm pɚhˈæps jˈutəlˌaɪzɪŋ/

text: snares and fast-moving projectiles.
ipa: /snˈɛɹz ənd fastmoving pɹədʒˈɛktəlz/

text: In fact, we know they fashioned and wielded many types of tools, sometimes affixing them
ipa: /ɪn fˈækt wˈi nˈoʊ ðˈeɪ fˈæʃənd ənd wˈildɪd mˈɛni tˈaɪps ˈʌv tˈulz səmtˈaɪmz əfˈɪksɪŋ ðˈɛm/

text: with glue they made from heated birch bark.
ipa: /wˈɪð ɡlˈu ðˈeɪ mˈeɪd fɹˈʌm hˈitəd bˈɝtʃ bˈɑɹk/

text: They also shaped hardwood digging sticks with fire and created reinforced, 3-ply string using bark fibers.
ipa: /ðˈeɪ ˈɔlsoʊ ʃˈeɪpt hˈɑɹdwˌʊd dˈɪɡɪŋ stˈɪks wˈɪð fˈaɪɚ ənd kɹiˈeɪtəd ɹˌiɪnfˈɔɹst 3ply stɹˈɪŋ jˈuzɪŋ bˈɑɹk fˈaɪbɚz/

text: Other findings have also raised questions about whether Neanderthals thought symbolically, seeing beyond direct utility, into
ipa: /ˈʌðɚ fˈaɪndɪŋz hˈæv ˈɔlsoʊ ɹˈeɪzd kwˈɛstʃənz əbˈaʊt wˈɛðɚ niˈændɚθˌɔlz θˈɔt sɪmbˈɑlɪkəli sˈiɪŋ bɪˈɑnd dɚˈɛkt jutˈɪləti ˈɪntu/

text: realms like art and language, long considered a hallmark of Homo sapiens.
ipa: /ɹˈɛlmz lˈaɪk ˈɑɹt ənd lˈæŋɡwədʒ lˈɔŋ kənsˈɪdɚd ə hˈɑlmˌɑɹk ˈʌv hˈoʊmoʊ sˈeɪpiənz/

text: Potentially for personal adornment, there’s evidence of Neanderthals selectively removing bird’s flight feathers, painting
ipa: /pətˈɛnʃəli fˈɔɹ pˈɝsɪnəl ədˈɔɹnmənt theres ˈɛvədəns ˈʌv niˈændɚθˌɔlz səlˈɛktɪvli ɹimˈuvɪŋ bˈɝdz flˈaɪt fˈɛðɚz pˈeɪntɪŋ/

text: and perforating shells, and wrapping eagle talons
ipa: /ənd pˈɝfɚˌeɪtɪŋ ʃˈɛlz ənd ɹˈæpɪŋ ˈiɡəl tˈælənz/

text: in what seems to have been another kind of animal tissue.
ipa: /ɪn wˈʌt sˈimz tˈu hˈæv bˈɪn ənˈʌðɚ kˈaɪnd ˈʌv ˈænəməl tˈɪsjˌu/

text: They likewise made markings on a giant elk’s toe bone
ipa: /ðˈeɪ lˈaɪkwˌaɪz mˈeɪd mˈɑɹkɪŋz ˈɑn ə dʒˈaɪənt ˈɛlks tˈoʊ bˈoʊn/

text: and created three cave paintings in Spain, if the original 65,000-year-old dating estimate holds.
ipa: /ənd kɹiˈeɪtəd θɹˈi kˈeɪv pˈeɪntɪŋz ɪn spˈeɪn ˈɪf ðə ɚˈɪdʒənəl 65000yearold dˈeɪtɪŋ ˈɛstəmət hˈoʊldz/

text: Meanwhile, broken, rearranged, and burned stalagmites deep within a French cave left scientists wondering
ipa: /mˈinwˌaɪl bɹˈoʊkən ɹˌiɚˈeɪndʒd ənd bˈɝnd stalagmites dˈip wɪðˈɪn ə fɹˈɛntʃ kˈeɪv lˈɛft sˈaɪəntɪsts wˈʌndɚɪŋ/

text: if the mysterious structures held spiritual or ceremonial significance to Neanderthals.
ipa: /ˈɪf ðə mɪstˈɪɹiəs stɹˈʌktʃɚz hˈɛld spˈɪɹɪtʃˌuəl ˈɔɹ sˌɛɹəmˈoʊniəl səɡnˈɪfɪkəns tˈu niˈændɚθˌɔlz/

text: Clearly, they weren’t as different as originally believed.
ipa: /klˈɪɹli ðˈeɪ werent ˈæz dˈɪfɚənt ˈæz ɚˈɪdʒənəli bɪlˈivd/

text: And following the first fully sequenced Neanderthal genome in 2010, researchers realized our species interbred.
ipa: /ənd fˈɑloʊɪŋ ðə fˈɝst fˈʊli sequenced niˈændɚθˌɔl dʒˈinˌoʊm ɪn 2010 ɹˈisɚtʃɚz ɹˈiəlˌaɪzd ˈaʊɚ spˈiʃiz ˌɪntɚbɹˈɛd/

text: All modern humans retain some Neanderthal DNA— up to about 4%— the result of hundreds
ipa: /ˈɔl mˈɑdɚn hjˈumənz ɹɪtˈeɪn sˈʌm niˈændɚθˌɔl dˈiˌɛnˈeɪ ˈʌp tˈu əbˈaʊt 4 ðə ɹɪzˈʌlt ˈʌv hˈʌndɹədz/

text: of discrete interbreeding events.
ipa: /ˈʌv dɪskɹˈit interbreeding ɪvˈɛnts/

text: So, what happened to Neanderthals?
ipa: /sˈoʊ wˈʌt hˈæpənd tˈu niˈændɚθˌɔlz/

text: Theories from rampant cannibalism, to disease and climate change, to aggressive Homo sapiens have been floated.
ipa: /θˈɪɹiz fɹˈʌm ɹˈæmpənt kˈænəbəlˌɪzəm tˈu dɪzˈiz ənd klˈaɪmət tʃˈeɪndʒ tˈu əɡɹˈɛsɪv hˈoʊmoʊ sˈeɪpiənz hˈæv bˈɪn flˈoʊtəd/

text: But another idea is that, because Neanderthals lived in smaller groups,
ipa: /bˈʌt ənˈʌðɚ aɪdˈiə ˈɪz ðˈæt bɪkˈɔz niˈændɚθˌɔlz lˈɪvd ɪn smˈɔlɚ ɡɹˈups/

text: as they interbred with larger populations of Homo sapiens, they just sort of got gradually absorbed.
ipa: /ˈæz ðˈeɪ ˌɪntɚbɹˈɛd wˈɪð lˈɑɹdʒɚ pˌɑpjəlˈeɪʃənz ˈʌv hˈoʊmoʊ sˈeɪpiənz ðˈeɪ dʒˈʌst sˈɔɹt ˈʌv ɡˈɑt ɡɹˈædʒuəli əbzˈɔɹbd/

text: Overall, consensus has begun shifting away from representing human evolution
ipa: /ˈoʊvɚˌɔl kənsˈɛnsəs hˈæz bɪɡˈʌn ʃˈɪftɪŋ əwˈeɪ fɹˈʌm ɹˌɛpɹɪzˈɛntɪŋ hjˈumən ˌɛvəlˈuʃən/

text: as tree-like and more towards a kind of braided stream, with different hominin groups separating
ipa: /ˈæz treelike ənd mˈɔɹ təwˈɔɹdz ə kˈaɪnd ˈʌv bɹˈeɪdɪd stɹˈim wˈɪð dˈɪfɚənt hominin ɡɹˈups sˈɛpɚˌeɪtɪŋ/

text: and rejoining at various junctures.
ipa: /ənd ɹidʒˈɔɪnɪŋ ˈæt vˈɛɹiəs dʒˈʌŋktʃɚz/

text: As we continue to learn more about our evolutionary cousins, each discovery raises questions about just
ipa: /ˈæz wˈi kəntˈɪnju tˈu lˈɝn mˈɔɹ əbˈaʊt ˈaʊɚ ˌɛvəlˈuʃənˌɛɹi kˈʌzənz ˈitʃ dɪskˈʌvɚi ɹˈeɪzəz kwˈɛstʃənz əbˈaʊt dʒˈʌst/

text: how much we share.
ipa: /hˈaʊ mˈʌtʃ wˈi ʃˈɛɹ/
